birth.stop: Villanova di Pordenone, birth in the Patriarchate
birth.date_confidence: Reconstructed. Treccani (Andrea Tilatti, DBI 79, 2013) says only Pordenone; the hamlet of Villanova is traditional attribution, correctly hedged. The year c. 1280 rests on a 2002 forensic examination of the partly mummified remains, which indicated a man of about fifty at death, and displaces the older proposals of 1265, 1274/75 and 1286. The Minor Planet Center naming citation for asteroid 4637 still prints 1265. Month and day are unknown and defaulted to 01-01.

stops.stop: Gemona del Friuli, a boy among the Friars Minor
stops.date_confidence: Act attested, identification contested. Treccani confirms the date, the place and the phrase verbatim: an act at Gemona del Friuli on 9 February 1296 naming an Odolricus puer fratrum Minorum. Tilatti calls the identification with the traveler attractive but not certain, so the claim is carried here as [R]. The research pool's two lenses disagree on the tag, one [A] and one [R], and the count of five friar-witnesses appears in one lens only and could not be sourced to Treccani.

stops.date_confidence: Tradition, not documented fact. The journey toward Pisa, the intention of sailing to Avignon for missionary reinforcements, and the dream of Francis ordering him back to his nest all come from later Franciscan hagiography (Wadding, Mark of Lisbon) as characterised by Tilatti. No contemporary document supports any of it. The month is an ordering device placing the attempt after the May dictation and before the January death.

stops.segment: Udine, the Body and the Cult
stops.stop: Udine, death at San Francesco
stops.date_confidence: Attested by Treccani: Monday, 14 January 1331, at the Franciscan convent of San Francesco, Udine. The weekday checks out against the Julian calendar. Two details in the research pool could not be confirmed in the Treccani text reached and are omitted from the campa: the named magistrate Conrad Bernardiggi and the crowd cutting at the habit and hair. Coordinates corrected to 46.0608, 13.2358, the church in Borgo Grazzano; the pool gave three different Udine pairs for the same building.

stops.segment: Udine, the Body and the Cult
stops.stop: Udine, the seventy miracles and the twenty-seven
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the month by Treccani: in May 1331 the Patriarch of Aquileia, Pagano della Torre, appointed a canon and a notary to take sworn testimony on reported healings at the tomb. Day unknown, defaulted to 01. The named officials (Melioranzi, Maffeo Cassini, the notary Guecelli) and the seventy-versus-twenty-seven discrepancy come from the geography lens of the research pool citing Tilatti.

stops.segment: Udine, the Body and the Cult
stops.stop: Udine, the stone sarcophagus
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the year by Treccani, which dates the commission and the elevation to 1332 without a month; the pool's 'May 1332' is unsupported and the month is defaulted to 01. Material corrected: Treccani says a stone sarcophagus, sarcofago di pietra, not alabaster; the pool's two lenses contradicted each other on this and stone is right. The reported presence of Beatrice of Bavaria, Countess of Gorizia, is not in the Treccani text reached and is not asserted here.

stops.segment: Udine, the Body and the Cult
stops.stop: Rome, the cult confirmed ab immemorabili
stops.date_confidence: Attested to the day by Treccani and corroborated by Wikipedia. The formal Roman inquiry into the immemorial cult opened in 1749. Odoric was of course never in Rome; the stop is placed here because the act is the disposition of his own cult and belongs to no other subject.

stops.stop: Santa Maria del Carmine, the relics moved
stops.date_confidence: Date corrected: Italian Wikipedia dates the transfer to the former Carmelite church to 1771, while 1769 is the year of the Venetian suppression of the religious houses; the research pool blurred the two into '1769-71'. Month and day unknown, defaulted to 01-01. Coordinates corrected to 46.0587, 13.2431, the Chiesa della Beata Vergine del Carmine on Via Aquileia, per Nominatim; the pool gave two other pairs, both roughly a kilometre off.

stops.segment: Udine, the Body and the Cult
stops.stop: Pordenone, the monument, the church, the asteroid
stops.date_confidence: Composite stop at the home pin, dated to the earliest of the three commemorations. The 1881 monument and the 1992 Mario Botta church are attested by the Wikipedia articles; asteroid 4637 Odorico was discovered at Chions, in the province of Pordenone, on 8 February 1989 by J. M. Baur, per the Minor Planet Center, whose naming citation prints the superseded birth year 1265. Month and day for the monument are unknown and defaulted to 01-01.
